    <text x="18" y="539" font-family="Poppins, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="400" fill="#B0B3B8">
      <tspan x="18" dy="0">The council voted 8–3 to expand overnight service on key bus and rail corridors, a move officials say will</tspan>
      <tspan x="18" dy="21">improve safety and give late-shift workers a more reliable way home. The plan includes additional lighting,</tspan>
      <tspan x="18" dy="21">camera coverage, and a smaller but more frequent fleet between 11 p.m. and 5 a.m. Riders have waited for</tspan>
      <tspan x="18" dy="21">months as the budget was finalized, but the proposal gained support after traffic data showed a 17% rise in</tspan>
      <tspan x="18" dy="21">late-night ridership since spring. Transit advocates applauded the decision, though some residents asked for</tspan>
      <tspan x="18" dy="21">clearer schedules and more frequent stops in outer neighborhoods. City staff will publish the rollout timeline</tspan>
      <tspan x="18" dy="21">next week, with the first routes expected to begin service on Sept. 1.</tspan>
    </text>
